intervals.label: laboratory constructed and in use
intervals.note: Constructed in 1997 in the Tentsuji Tunnel for ultra-rare-process nuclear spectroscopy; experiments ELEGANT V (from April 1997) and ELEGANT VI (from November 1997) are listed. No source read says whether the observatory is still in use; the latest activity read is the PICO-LON measurement started in September 2007.
intervals.quote: has been constructed in the center of the tunnel which location is about 100 km south from Osaka University for ultra rare process nuclear spectroscopy in 1997.

name: Oto Cosmo Observatory
notes: Located in the Tentsuji Tunnel (5 km) between Oto village and Nishiyoshino village in Nara prefecture, about 100 km south of Osaka (RCNP annual report).
Created by the nai-rest stream for ELEGANT V and the early PICO-LON measurements; no website of the observatory was found (the RCNP group page is the closest official description).

operator_text.quote: Research Center for Nuclear Physics, Osaka University
operator_text.value: Research Center for Nuclear Physics (RCNP), Osaka University

depth.note: PICO-LON papers quote about 1200 m.w.e. (arXiv:astro-ph/0611700) and the RCNP group page about 470 m maximum depth; the 2001 annual report of the observatory is followed.
depth.quote: The maximum depth of the tunnel is about 500 m (1400 m w.e.).

summary.plain: A small underground laboratory of Osaka University in the middle of a road tunnel in Nara prefecture, Japan, about 100 km south of Osaka. Dark matter and double-beta-decay detectors of the ELEGANT series ran there from 1997.
summary.technical: RCNP (Osaka University) Oto Cosmo Observatory in the centre of the 5 km Tentsuji Tunnel between Oto village and Nishiyoshino village, Nara; maximum overburden about 500 m (1400 m.w.e.), cosmic-ray flux 1e-7 cm^-2 s^-1, radon about 10 Bq/m3; experimental rooms 3 km from the Oto entrance.
